messages:
amy: Customer hitting intermittent 500s + spikes on /v1/generate. They provided a request_id: req_0a1b2c3d. Errors started ~2026-03-15T18:10:00Z and recur ~every 2 min. Can SRE scan server logs/ingest for that req id? :eyes:
ben: Thanks — can you paste the exact request_id and timezone you saw that in? Also which region (us-west-2 / eu-west-1)?
amy: request_id = req_0a1b2c3d, seen in us-west-2. Customer org: acme-inc, sample client-side curl they ran attached (sanitized).
sri: Copy. I'll try a quick Kibana/KQL search. Note: our long-term log retention for request traces is 30 days; anything older may be gone unless archived. If logs are expired we'll need a debug bundle from the customer (stack traces + client headers) or link to our proxy traces.
ben: If SRI can't find server logs, we can ask them to repro and give a debug bundle including a fresh request_id + full curl. Also check billing note: some 5xx patterns correlate with quota/billing failures returning 402 earlier in the flow, but that usually shows up in proxy logs.
sri: Running KQL now. Typical KQL for this: `request_id:"req_0a1b2c3d" OR json.request_id:"req_0a1b2c3d"` — widen to `trace_id` if needed. Also try time window `@timestamp:[2026-03-15T18:08:00 TO 2026-03-15T18:20:00]`.
sri: If you prefer internal CLI: `logs search --request-id req_0a1b2c3d --start "2026-03-15T18:05:00Z" --end "2026-03-15T18:25:00Z" --region us-west-2`
amy: I ran a quick corner search and found only proxy logs (502) but no backend GPU runtime stack traces. Could be that the request was short-lived or hit a fallback layer.
ben: Also try this Kibana query to catch encoded cases: `message: /req_0a1b2c3d/ OR context.request.id: req_0a1b2c3d` — some services write the id to different fields.
sri: Found some entries at 18:11:12 for the ingress LB: `upstream reset` then `rpc timeout`. No model-worker logs for that id — could be worker recycled. Two paths: 1) ask customer for a fresh repro with `--header "x-request-id: req_new..."` and their full curl so we can correlate; or 2) escalate to infra to check node-level journald for that time range (may have more ephemeral logs not indexed). Which do you want?
amy: Customer is impatient, wants root cause quickly. Ask infra and I'll request a fresh repro as backup.
sri: Ok escalating to infra. tagging ben for infra handoff. ben: Pinging infra oncall — @ben-pager — can you check node logs on us-west-2 around 2026-03-15T18:08-18:15Z for requests matching `req_0a1b2c3d`? Look for `OOM`, `worker restart`, or `rpc timeout` entries. If logs are missing from ES index, check raw node journal and s3 archive.
kibana-bot: Kibana search saved: https://kibana.internal.redwood/search/req_0a1b2c3d — results expire in 24h.
ben: infra oncall acknowledged, will pull journald and s3 slices. If infra finds nothing (expired), we'll ask customer for a debug bundle and a new request_id plus full curl and timestamps, and offer to run a repro from our end with their prompt.
amy: I'll message customer: please run the curl below and share the new `x-request-id` header/response, and also attach a HAR or verbose curl output. Sample repro we asked them to run:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-request-id: req_customer_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"small prompt","max_tokens":64}'
```
amy: Request also asked them to include exact client local time + timezone and whether they're behind a corporate proxy.
sri: Note for support: if logs are older than 30 days and not in s3 archive, we can still pull partial traces from the trace-service for ~90 days but not full worker stdout. Mentioned to ben.
ben: thanks — I'll follow up when infra returns findings. :thumbsup:
amy: thanks everyone — keeping customer updated. :white_check_mark:
